How It Works

How Professional School Cleaning Works

Our school cleaning process follows a systematic, six-step protocol designed to maximize pathogen elimination and provide verifiable documentation of results. Every step is performed by trained, background-checked technicians.

1
Classroom Sanitization

Every classroom receives daily desk and chair disinfection, floor vacuuming or mopping, whiteboard cleaning, high-touch surface treatment (door handles, light switches, shared devices), and trash removal — all using Green Seal certified, non-toxic products.

2
Restroom Deep Cleaning

School restrooms receive full cleaning twice daily minimum (morning and afternoon) with mid-day spot checks in high-enrollment buildings. Each cleaning covers fixture sanitization, floor disinfection, supply replenishment, and mirror cleaning with ATP verification of high-touch surfaces.

3
Cafeteria Service

Cafeteria cleaning occurs after each meal service — not just at end of day. Tables and benches are sanitized, floors swept and mopped, food service areas wiped down, and trash removed. Monthly deep cleaning includes vent hood degreasing and behind-equipment cleaning.

4
Gymnasium and Athletic Areas

Gym floors receive daily dust-mopping with weekly machine scrubbing. Locker rooms and shower areas are disinfected daily with products effective against MRSA and fungal infections. Athletic equipment surfaces are wiped between uses when day porter service is included.

5
Seasonal Deep Cleaning

Summer, winter, and spring breaks provide windows for floor stripping and refinishing, carpet extraction, window washing, light fixture cleaning, HVAC vent cleaning, and furniture deep cleaning that cannot be performed during the school year.

6
Documentation and Reporting

Every cleaning session is documented through JaniTrack with timestamped photos, ATP readings, and task completion records. Administrators access reports through a dashboard that provides the documentation trail health inspectors and school boards require.

FAQ

School Cleaning FAQ — North Bergen, NJ

Common questions about school cleaning services in North Bergen.

What is professional school cleaning?+
Professional school cleaning refers to specialized janitorial and sanitization services designed for K-12 schools and educational facilities. It differs from standard commercial cleaning by requiring CDC-compliant disinfection protocols, exclusively non-toxic products safe for children, scheduling flexibility around academic calendars, and documented compliance for health department inspections. Professional school cleaning covers classrooms, cafeterias, restrooms, gymnasiums, administrative areas, and specialty spaces like science labs and art rooms.
How often should schools be professionally cleaned?+
Schools require daily cleaning during the academic year including classroom sanitization, restroom deep cleaning (twice daily minimum), cafeteria cleaning after each meal, and high-touch surface disinfection. Restrooms in high-enrollment schools need mid-day spot checks. Seasonal deep cleaning during summer, winter, and spring breaks addresses floor refinishing, carpet extraction, window washing, and HVAC maintenance that cannot be performed while school is in session.
What cleaning products are safe for schools?+
School environments require Green Seal certified or EPA Safer Choice products that are non-toxic, fragrance-free, and allergy-safe. These products meet CDC guidelines for educational facility disinfection while avoiding the VOCs, fragrances, and chemical irritants that trigger asthma and allergies in children. GreenPoint uses exclusively certified products in all school facilities — we never substitute conventional products regardless of availability.
Are you approved to clean NYC public schools?+
Yes. GreenPoint Maintenance Services is an NYC DOE Approved Vendor, authorized to provide cleaning products and services to New York City public schools. We are also MBE/MWBE certified with NYC SBS and New York State, and SAM.gov registered for federal contracts. Every dollar spent with GreenPoint counts toward your school or district's diversity procurement targets.
How do you verify cleaning quality in schools?+
Our JaniTrack system provides objective verification through timestamped, GPS-tagged photo documentation of every cleaning session, ATP bioluminescence testing that scientifically measures surface cleanliness, digital task completion checklists, and periodic supervisor audits. School administrators access all reports through an online dashboard — providing the documentation trail that health inspectors, school boards, and parents expect.
Can you clean around the school schedule?+
Yes. We offer after-hours (evening), overnight, and weekend cleaning that never disrupts instructional time. Day porter services are available during school hours for restroom monitoring, cafeteria turnovers, and spill response. Summer deep cleaning programs are planned months in advance to maximize the break window. Our scheduling adapts to your academic calendar, exam periods, event schedules, and building access policies.
How much does school cleaning cost?+
School cleaning typically ranges from $0.08-$0.18 per square foot per cleaning visit depending on facility size, age, cleaning frequency, and scope. A typical 30,000 sq ft elementary school cleaned 5 days per week runs approximately $3,000-$6,000 per month. Summer deep cleaning is priced separately as a project. We provide detailed, scope-specific proposals after a complimentary facility walkthrough — never generic estimates.
